title: French President Emmanuel Macron Calls on YouTube to Finance Content and Warns of Growing Threat to Cultural Model (EXCLUSIVE)
content:
Macron said the Lumière Summit in Saint-Paul-de-Vence was deliberately being held at a moment of dramatic upheaval for the entertainment business, from the growing dominance of YouTube and TikTok to AI.

ByElsa Keslassy

International Correspondent

French PresidentEmmanuel Macronsaid the Lumière Summit in Saint-Paul-de-Vence, which he co-chaired with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Monday, was deliberately held at a moment of dramatic upheaval for the entertainment business, from the growing dominance ofYouTubeand TikTok to AI and media consolidation.

Speaking toVarietyat the event, he pointed to the growing power of YouTube, TikTok and other social platforms as one of the reasons the timing was right for the landmark gathering devoted to the future of cinema and the moving image.

“YouTube is very efficient. It’s de facto the default platform in a lot of countries for a lot of people. And it’s quite clear that today they divert a lot of people from these platforms or the big channels where a lot of money is invested in creation,” said Macron at the Fondation Maeght, a French art foundation showcasing works of art from Georges Braque to Joan Miró, nestled amid a luxuriant forest.

French President Emmanuel Macron on the growing global reach of YouTube:pic.twitter.com/NM9yWRf6i3

He argued that YouTube, which is currently outtalking Netflix in over 20 international markets, should increasingly be brought into the same ecosystem as other global platforms such as Netflix, Amazon and Disney, that have been required to invest in local production.

France and other countries need to “engage with them” in a multilateral way, he said, to try to change the platform’s approach so that it helps finance “local content,” while supporting “more creativity, more creations, more respect of the authors.”

Macron, who’s been a driving force behind the rise of French AI companies, including Mistral, as well as the creation of the EU’s AI Act and the international summit on AI that was held last year, also said France wanted to compete aggressively in AI by expanding computing capacity, data centers and European models. But he insisted that technological ambition must be accompanied by protections for intellectual property and much greater transparency.

Asked about his discussions about EU regulations with companies such as Google or OpenAI, Macron said that while France is eager to compete in the AI race, it’s also pushing for greater transparency and protections for creators in Europe.

“When you have content produced by AI, you just have to know it. So transparency for us is key,” he said. “We want to flag when the content is produced with AI. Because we think it’s fair.”

Without that, Macron warned, AI could “totally transform the relationship to truth,” feeding distrust not only in creative content but in science and democracy.

Macron also addressed the increasing consolidation of the entertainment business and his discussions surrounding the greenlighting of the Paramount-Warner Bros. deal by the EU regulators. He said he didn’t have an active role in lobbying for the merger, but admitted that he supported “the commitments made to invest more in Europe and to create more content and to provide guarantees and commitments vis-à-vis our theaters.” Paramount Skydance boss David Ellisontraveled to Paris (as well as London and Germany) in January and met with Macron, among other high-level political and industry figures.

The French President described the merger case as fundamentally “a U.S. M&A story,” saying his priority was ensuring that a major company like Paramount Skydance maintained a strong footprint in France and Europe. While Ellison wasn’t present at theLumiere Summit, Paramount Skydance’s Andy Gordon was there and sat at Macron’s table at lunch, alongside The Walt Disney Company’s Dana Walden, Netflix’s Ted Sarandos, NBCUniversal Entertainment’s Donna Langley, Mediawan’s Pierre-Antoine Capton and Sony’s Tom Rothman, among others.

“What is important to us is to make sure that you will still finance creation, that you will still work with us, that you will still make more movies in France and in Europe,” he said.

The Summit is also being held on the last stretch of his second mandate as he is due to leave office in May. With the far-right and far-left parties dominating polls ahead of the next presidential election, the French film and TV industry has shared deep concerns over the future of France’s prized cultural model that could come under threat.

Asked what would survive beyond 2027, Macron pointed first to France’s international tax credit for international movies and TV series, which was recently strengthened with the inclusion of above-the-line costs and has helped draw a growing number of major U.S. and international productions to the country.

“We improved tax credits, international tax credits. If somebody wants to withdraw this tax credit, it will just kill the industry and a lot of opportunities,” said Macron, who had toldVarietyin a cover interview in 2024 that he would fight for “Emily in Paris” Season 5 to remain in the French capital, prompting a comedic feud with the Rome mayor. Besides the sixth and final season of “Emily in Paris,” “The White Lotus” season 4 is also currently shooting in France.

He also pointed to the investment made during his presidency in studios and production infrastructure as part of his France 2030 plan, which he said has turned France into a leading international shooting destination.

“We want more of them to make new movies in our country. Why? Because it’s good for our ecosystem,” he said. “It will hire a lot of technicians and actors and so on. It will show our landscapes, and it will create jobs during the movie is made and it will attract a lot of people in our landscapes and our cities and so on.”

Yet, Macron suggested the bigger battle after his departure could be over the foundations of France’s cultural policy itself.

“Some extremes are fighting very hard against the CNC (National Film Board) and what we call this exception culturelle and the DNA of the French model,” Macron said. France’s system, developed over decades, uses levies on cinema admissions that are collected by the National Film Board and re-injected into local production, alongside other schemes supporting independent producers, filmmakers and theaters.

“We have to be ready to resist because this model has been created during decades by a lot of artists, by the state and the different governments and it’s extremely important,” he said.

Ultimately, Macron tied the defense of the French model not only to jobs and filmmaking but also to the country’s soft power.

“Culture and art is part of what France is, but it’s part as well of our soft power outside,” he said. “Recognizing that art is an exception which requires specific investment of the government, diversity of people, players, authors, protection of their rights and a specific effort in terms of multilateralism is crucial.”
title_zh: 法國總統艾曼紐·馬克龍(Emmanuel Macron)呼籲YouTube資助內容，並警告文化模式面臨日益嚴重的威脅（獨家）。
content_zh:
法國總統艾曼紐·馬克龍(Emmanuel Macron)表示，在聖保羅德旺斯舉行的盧米埃峰會(Lumière Summit)故意選在娛樂產業劇變的時刻舉行，這一變化包括YouTube和TikTok的日益主導地位，以及人工智慧和媒體整合的影響。

在活動中，他對《綜藝》(Variety)表示，YouTube、TikTok及其他社交平台的日益強大是這次專注於電影和動態影像未來的重大聚會時機正確的原因之一。

馬克龍在法國馬格基金會(Fondation Maeght)發言時指出：“YouTube非常有效。對於很多國家來說，它事實上是許多人使用的默認平台。而且很明顯，今天他們將很多人從這些平台或大量資金投入創作的大頻道中引開。”

他主張，YouTube目前在超過20個國際市場的影響力超過Netflix，應該越來越多地被納入與Netflix、亞馬遜(Amazon)和迪士尼(Disney)等其他全球平台相同的生態系統，這些平台被要求投資於本地製作。

馬克龍表示，法國和其他國家需要以多邊的方式“與他們互動”，以試圖改變該平台的做法，使其有助於資助“本地內容”，同時支持“更多創意、更多創作，更尊重作者”。

馬克龍一直是法國人工智慧公司（如Mistral）崛起的推動者，也是歐盟人工智慧法案的創建者，以及去年舉行的國際人工智慧峰會的參與者。他還表示，法國希望在人工智慧領域積極競爭，擴大計算能力、數據中心和歐洲模型。但他堅持認為，技術雄心必須伴隨著對知識產權的保護和更大的透明度。

在被問及與谷歌(Google)或OpenAI等公司的EU規範討論時，馬克龍表示，儘管法國渴望在人工智慧競賽中競爭，但也在推動對創作者的更大透明度和保護。

他說：“當你有由人工智慧生成的內容時，你必須知道這一點。因此，對我們來說，透明度是關鍵。我們希望標示出何時內容是由人工智慧生成的，因為我們認為這是公平的。”

馬克龍警告，如果沒有這一點，人工智慧可能會“徹底改變與真相的關係”，引發對創意內容、科學和民主的不信任。

馬克龍(Emmanuel Macron)也談到了娛樂業日益集中的情況，以及他與歐盟監管機構就派拉蒙-華納兄弟(Paramount-Warner Bros.)合併案的討論。他表示自己並未積極參與這一合併的遊說，但承認他支持“對於在歐洲投資更多、創造更多內容以及對我們的影院提供保證和承諾的承諾。”派拉蒙天際(PARAMOUNT SKYDANCE)的負責人大衛·艾利森(David Ellison)在一月前往巴黎（以及倫敦和德國），並與馬克龍及其他高層政治和行業人士會面。

法國總統將這一合併案描述為根本上“一個美國的併購故事”，並表示他的首要任務是確保像派拉蒙天際這樣的大公司在法國和歐洲保持強大的影響力。雖然艾利森並未出席盧米埃峰會，但派拉蒙天際的安迪·戈登(Andy Gordon)在場，並與馬克龍共進午餐，還有華特迪士尼公司(The Walt Disney Company)的達娜·沃爾登(Dana Walden)、奈飛(Netflix)的泰德·薩蘭多斯(Ted Sarandos)、NBC環球娛樂(NBCUniversal Entertainment)的唐娜·蘭利(Donna Langley)、Mediawan的皮埃爾-安托萬·卡普頓(Pierre-Antoine Capton)和索尼(Sony)的湯姆·羅斯曼(Tom Rothman)等人。

他表示：“對我們來說，重要的是確保你們仍然會資助創作，仍然會與我們合作，仍然會在法國和歐洲拍攝更多電影。”

此次峰會正值他第二任期的最後階段，他將於五月離任。在即將到來的總統選舉中，極右派和極左派政黨在民調中占據主導地位，法國電影和電視產業對法國珍貴的文化模式未來的深切擔憂可能會受到威脅。

當被問及2027年之後什麼會存活下來時，馬克龍首先提到了法國對國際電影和電視劇的國際稅收抵免，該抵免最近通過包括上線成本而得到了加強，並幫助吸引越來越多的美國和國際大型製作進入法國。

馬克龍表示：“我們改善了稅收抵免，國際稅收抵免。如果有人想撤回這項稅收抵免，這將會摧毀這個行業和許多機會。”他在2024年對《綜藝雜誌》(Variety)的封面專訪中曾表示，他將為《艾蜜莉在巴黎》(Emily in Paris)第五季留在法國首都而奮鬥，這引發了與羅馬市長的喜劇性爭執。除了《艾蜜莉在巴黎》第六季和最後一季外，《白蓮花》(The White Lotus)第四季也正在法國拍攝。

他還提到了在其總統任期內對製片廠和製作基礎設施的投資，作為其法國2030計劃的一部分，他表示這使法國成為一個領先的國際拍攝地點。

他說：“我們希望更多的製作人在我們的國家拍攝新電影。為什麼？因為這對我們的生態系統有好處。”他補充道：“這將雇用大量技術人員和演員等，展示我們的風景，並在拍攝期間創造就業機會，吸引許多人來到我們的風景和城市等地。”

然而，馬克宏(Emmanuel Macron)暗示，他離開後更大的戰鬥可能是關於法國文化政策本身的基礎。

馬克宏說：“一些極端勢力正在非常努力地對抗國家電影局(CNC, Centre National du Cinéma et de l'Image Animée)以及我們所稱的文化例外(exception culturelle)和法國模式的DNA。” 法國的這一系統經過數十年發展，利用從電影票房中徵收的稅款，這些稅款由國家電影局收集並重新注入當地製作，還有其他支持獨立製片人、電影製作人和劇院的計劃。

他表示：“我們必須準備好抵抗，因為這一模式是由許多藝術家、國家和不同政府在數十年內創建的，這是極其重要的。”

最終，馬克宏將保護法國模式的辯護不僅與就業和電影製作聯繫在一起，還與國家的軟實力相關。

他說：“文化和藝術是法國的一部分，但它也是我們在外部的軟實力的一部分。承認藝術是一種例外，需要政府的特定投資、多樣化的人員、參與者、作者、保護他們的權利，以及在多邊主義方面的特定努力是至關重要的。”
summary_zh: 法國總統艾曼紐·馬克龍(Emmanuel Macron)表示，在聖保羅德旺斯舉行的盧米埃峰會(Lumière Summit)故意選在娛樂產業劇變的時刻舉行，這一變化包括YouTube和TikTok的日益主導地位，以及人工智慧和媒體整合的影響。
